key_insight: FK-ReMask guides pretrained crystal diffusion models toward multiple target properties by steering both crystal geometry and chemical composition without retraining.
engineering_relevance: The method could help screen candidate photovoltaic materials against several physical requirements in a single generation workflow.
method: Maintain multiple denoising trajectories and replicate promising candidates using Feynman–Kac particle selection.
Re-mask committed atom types so candidates can explore alternative chemical compositions.
Apply gradient-free property steering entirely at inference time.
evidence_signal: Across four electronic, photovoltaic, and mechanical objectives, the abstract reports improved yield of stable, unique, novel and property-on-target materials, plus joint steering of three photovoltaic properties.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical gains or experimental solar-cell validation, so device-level benefits remain unestablished.
paper_title: Multi-property Feynman-Kac Steering of Crystal Diffusion Models
